The record notes that the switch did not change the balance of party representation in the Chamber of Deputies, while a recent election in Maranhão had added a seat to the MDB and reduced ARENA’s representation. The subject is party organization and alignment rather than election administration or legislative proceedings, within the period of Brazil’s military regime and its restricted two-party system.

It also reflects institutional and legal questions affecting state politics, including the Supreme Court’s ruling on the constitutionality of extending a governor’s term. Read against the military governments established after the 1964 coup, these records document state-level political competition and the limits within which electoral activity continued under military rule. The catalogue excludes elections of state or local persons to national office, which are classified under POL 14.
